hypothesis: Explicit neighboring-frame information improves unseen-content event transfer and state robustness relative to an otherwise identical capacity-matched per-frame control.
rationale: The frozen V3 model is per-frame and cannot explicitly compare adjacent frames.
P2 onset admission collapsed, but chords and PalmMute also show state failures, so an onset-head-only intervention cannot test the full observed failure.
The combined diagnostic recorded descriptive neighboring-frame evidence but did not establish causality.
A controlled input intervention can test temporal information while holding architecture, parameter count, optimizer, loss, decoder and thresholds constant.

candidate.name: temporal_triplet
candidate.edgeRule: replicate x[t] for any missing neighbor at crop boundary
candidate.model: 576->128 ReLU shared encoder; 6x21 state head; 6 onset-logit head
candidate.loss: same explicit event loss and weights as tiny_fit_pilot_v1

comparator.name: capacity_matched_repeated_current
comparator.model: identical 576->128 ReLU shared encoder; identical heads
comparator.purpose: Controls for parameter count and input width; the sole information difference is access to neighboring frames.

initialization.rule: Candidate and comparator use identical initial weights within each fold.

population.source: the same already-exposed 4 P1 + 4 homologous P2 direct-input 200-frame development crops only
population.claimBoundary: All P1/P2 examples are development data. No performer holdout exists in this experiment.

split.rule: For each fold, both P1 and P2 views of the held-out content group are excluded from fitting and used only for that fold's evaluation.
split.trainingPerFold: 6 captures from the other three content groups
split.evaluationPerFold: 2 captures: P1 and P2 of the held-out content group
split.interpretation: Tests unseen-content transfer within already-examined performers only; does not test unseen-performer generalization.

primary: boundary-corrected event precision/recall/F1 per held-out capture and macro across all 8 held-out evaluations
secondary: source-attack onset recall at exact center and fixed +/-2 separately
true-state admission/error on source-defined attack frames
true-state accuracy on active non-attack/sustain frames
repeated-attack numerator/denominator and recall when present

criteria: candidate macro boundary-corrected event F1 >= comparator macro F1 + 0.10
candidate repeated-attack recall >= 0.60 when repeated held-out references exist
candidate real-audio silence/non-active false-admission rate is not higher than comparator by more than 0.01 absolute
candidate held-out true-state accuracy is not lower than comparator by more than 0.02 absolute
all metrics finite and unresolved labels = 0
positiveProbeCriteria.note: These are probe advancement criteria only. Passing does not establish performer generalization or customer readiness.

stopConditions: Stop a model at 125 optimizer steps even if still improving.
No extra epochs, learning-rate changes, threshold rescue, alternate context widths, architecture sweep, or automatic retry.
If preparation/identity guards fail, stop before optimizer work.
If candidate fails positiveProbeCriteria, record and stop this hypothesis.
If candidate passes, next step is design-only for a separately authorized performer-generalization evaluation; P3 remains sealed.

causalInterpretation.pass: Supports the hypothesis that explicit neighboring-frame information is useful beyond equal-capacity per-frame input on this P1/P2 unseen-content development test.
causalInterpretation.fail: Does not support this fixed triplet-context intervention under the frozen budget; do not infer that all temporal models are ineffective.
prohibitedClaims: temporal context is the unique causal mechanism
